title: Hypergonadotropic Hypogonadism: Klinefelter Syndrome 47,XXY, Dysgenesis and Hormone Replacement
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology

steps.say: Primary gonadal failure releases anterior pituitary gonadotropins from normal steroid feedback inhibition.
steps.tx: Recognize primary testicular failure by evaluating the **Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism hallmark** profile on laboratory testing. Characterized by primary gonadal failure with markedly elevated serum gonadotropins (FSH and LH > 20-40 IU/L) due to absence of negative feedback from sex steroids and inhibin B.

vis.alt: Medical illustration of hypergonadotropic hypogonadism showing pituitary LH and FSH hypersecretion, atrophic small testis, and histological seminiferous tubule hyalinisation and fibrosis.
vis.caption: Testicular histological dysgenesis, seminiferous tubule fibrosis, and elevated gonadotropins in hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

steps.say: Meiotic nondisjunction generates the most prevalent constitutional sex chromosome aneuploidy in newborn boys.
steps.tx: Assess epidemiology and cytogenetics by determining **Klinefelter syndrome 47,XXY incidence** in neonatal screening statistics. Klinefelter syndrome is the most common sex-chromosome aneuploidy in males (1 in 500-600 liveborn boys), caused by meiotic non-disjunction of paternal or maternal X chromosomes during gametogenesis.

vis.title: Cytogenetic Features of Klinefelter Syndrome
rows: Most common genetic cause of male hypogonadism
Increased risk correlated with advanced maternal age

steps.say: Progressive hyalinization of seminiferous tubules during adolescence results in characteristic eunuchoid proportions.
steps.tx: Identify physical features during pubertal examination noting **Pubertal phenotype and testicular fibrosclerosis** in adolescent males. Adolescents develop eunuchoid proportions (tall stature, long legs, span > height by 5 cm), bilateral firm small testes (< 4-6 mL) due to progressive hyalinization of seminiferous tubules, and gynecomastia in 50-80%.

vis.alt: Diagram of the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis illustrating GnRH pulse generator, LH stimulation of Leydig cells, FSH drive to Sertoli cells, and negative feedback loops.
vis.caption: Hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis showing negative feedback regulation disrupted in primary gonadal failure.

steps.say: Adolescents and adults carry distinct risks for malignant neoplasms alongside cardiometabolic complications.
steps.tx: Screen for long term systemic comorbidities by reviewing **Endocrine and metabolic comorbidities** during annual follow up visits. Adults with Klinefelter carry a 20-fold increased risk of male breast cancer, 5-fold risk of metabolic syndrome/type 2 diabetes, extragonadal germ cell tumors (mediastinal teratoma), and mitral valve prolapse.

steps.say: Exogenous testosterone replacement builds peak bone mass and preserves lean muscle during pubertal maturation.
steps.tx: Initiate androgen replacement by following established **Testosterone replacement timing** guidelines in symptomatic adolescents. Testosterone replacement therapy is initiated at age 12-14 years when serum testosterone plateaus and LH/FSH rise, building bone mineral density, lean muscle mass, and preventing metabolic syndrome.

left.title: Initiation Regimen (Age 12-14)
points: 50 mg IM monthly, titrated over 2-3 years
Allows physiological virilization without rapid closure

right.title: Adult Maintenance Targets
points: Full adult replacement (200-250 mg every 2-3 weeks)
Maintains normal adult male testosterone levels

steps.say: Surgical sperm retrieval before complete testicular hyalinization offers biological paternity opportunities.
steps.tx: Preserve future fertility options through timely **Microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE)** in late adolescence. Micro-TESE achieves viable sperm retrieval rates of 40-50% in non-mosaic Klinefelter adolescents and young adults for intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), before complete testicular sclerosis occurs. Early cryopreservation allows biological parenthood.

steps.say: Exogenous insults including ionizing radiation and cytotoxic chemotherapy cause irreversible gonadal failure.
steps.tx: Evaluate non-genetic secondary insults by investigating **Acquired hypergonadotropic hypogonadism causes** in pediatric oncology survivors. Secondary testicular failure can result from bilateral testicular torsion, mumps orchitis, radiation (> 20 Gy to testes destroys Sertoli and Leydig cells), or alkylating chemotherapy (cyclophosphamide > 200-300 mg/kg).

vis.title: Acquired Etiologies of Primary Testicular Failure
rows: Permanent Leydig and Sertoli cell destruction
Severe germ cell aplasia with azoospermia

steps.say: Transient physiological glandular enlargement regresses spontaneously in the majority of adolescent boys.
steps.tx: Distinguish self-limiting pubertal changes from pathology through **Persistent pubertal gynecomastia management** protocols. Physiological pubertal gynecomastia affects up to 60% of boys at Tanner stages 2-3, spontaneously regressing in 90% within 1-2 years; refractory severe cases (> 4 cm diameter) respond to tamoxifen or subcutaneous mastectomy.

Reassurance: Spontaneous Regression in 90% in 1-2 Years
